evidence/body.name: agency-dispatch-mode-work
evidence/body.body:
`futon3c/scripts/agency_send.py` without `--mode work` lets the server classify the packet by regex (`http.clj` `invoke-job-mode`: only "mode: task", "task assignment", "fm-NNN", "falsify/prove/counterexample/state of play" → work); everything else runs as **brief**, which skips execution-evidence enforcement (`README-ground-control.md:40`). Discovered 2026-08-30 when D1 (P-find-over-snatch) came back `"mode":"brief"` although it writes and commits a file. The CLAUDE.md dispatch recipe does not mention the flag.

**Why:** brief mode means the job can complete without the server checking that tools actually ran — exactly the paraphrase-as-citation / self-report facade the lifecycle is meant to refuse.
**How to apply:** `--from claude-15 --to <seat> --kind bell --mode work --park --park-deadline 2700` on every dispatch that reads code or writes files; check `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/<id>` shows `mode: work` (~5 s after send). See [[formal-war-machine-locations]].

**Also on this script (2026-10-20):** `--requisition` must read `"<M-|E-|T-><name> — <purpose>"`; a bare packet label ("M10b-1 — …") is rejected, and the rejection prints *after* the park-lane notice, so the output looks as if the bell went. For wm-contract packets write `"M-wm-contract — M10b-1 …"`. After any send error, check the seat's job list before resending. See [[kimi-unique-requisition]] for the Kimi variant.

**2026-11-03:** `futon3c/scripts/bell-file.sh` has no `--mode`; packets sent through it run as `brief` too. For packets that must execute, send the file on stdin to `agency_send.py --mode work < packet.md` (stdin redirect is expansion-safe, like a quoted heredoc).

evidence/body.body:
`futon3c/scripts/agency_send.py` without `--mode work` lets the server classify the packet by regex (`http.clj` `invoke-job-mode`: only "mode: task", "task assignment", "fm-NNN", "falsify/prove/counterexample/state of play" → work); everything else runs as **brief**, which skips execution-evidence enforcement (`README-ground-control.md:40`). Discovered 2026-08-30 when D1 (P-find-over-snatch) came back `"mode":"brief"` although it writes and commits a file. The CLAUDE.md dispatch recipe does not mention the flag.

**Why:** brief mode means the job can complete without the server checking that tools actually ran — exactly the paraphrase-as-citation / self-report facade the lifecycle is meant to refuse.
**How to apply:** `--from claude-15 --to <seat> --kind bell --mode work --park --park-deadline 2700` on every dispatch that reads code or writes files; check `GET /api/alpha/invoke/jobs/<id>` shows `mode: work` (~5 s after send). See [[formal-war-machine-locations]].

**Also on this script (2026-10-20):** `--requisition` must read `"<M-|E-|T-><name> — <purpose>"`; a bare packet label ("M10b-1 — …") is rejected, and the rejection prints *after* the park-lane notice, so the output looks as if the bell went. For wm-contract packets write `"M-wm-contract — M10b-1 …"`. After any send error, check the seat's job list before resending. See [[kimi-unique-requisition]] for the Kimi variant.

evidence/body.hook: If an action needs no judgement, take it directly — don't send a notification asking someone else to.
evidence/body.name: no-judgement-means-act
evidence/body.body:
When the remedy for a detected condition involves no judgement, perform it.
Do not raise a notice, a followup, a queue entry or an escalation asking a
person or another agent to do it.

**Why:** Joe, 2026-09-18, on unpushed commits — "I don't even see why unpushed
commits needs a notification rather than a direct classical action. No
judgement is involved." A notice for something nobody has to decide is just a
queue that waits, and waiting work decays. The library already ruled this:
`inbox-zero/escalate-by-who-can-act` puts ordinary accumulation at tier 0,
which acts without asking anyone.

**How to apply:** split by whether a person must decide something. Ten dirty
files INFORM (deciding what is yours and whether to keep it needs a person);
ten unpushed commits ACT (the commit is already written; pushing decides
nothing). Report the *failures* of the direct action instead — a rejected
push is someone else's history to reconcile, and that does need a person.

**Dispatching a drafted packet is also tier 0** (Joe, 2026-10-21, on S4d):
"I don't see why this was a question for me. Thinking of it that way cost
hours." CLAUDE.md already makes belling to an idle Codex seat the default;
once a packet is drafted and reviewed, send it and park, then report the
job-id. Ending a turn on "Shall I dispatch?" leaves the work idle until Joe
happens to read it.

Related: thresholds here are counts, never ages — a staleness window on a
bare-metal box is not a safety margin, it is how long the work is allowed to
sit unsaved. See [[fix-dont-disable]] and [[own-your-own-breakage]].

# Review request: 40ºBelowDB (minus40), work so far and the plan

build step. No code changes are asked of you; read and comment.

## What it is

40ºBelowDB is a local memory store for agents, specified by Joe on 2026-10-09
(`~/code/minus40/docs/spec-2026-10-09.txt`). Joe chose Claude Code's own
memories (`~/.claude/projects/*/memory/*.md`, 294 files) as the data source,
and the long-term aim is to replace Claude's file memory ("hot memory") with
this store ("cool memory"). Repo: `~/code/minus40` (local, no remote). The
README there has every command and result; `docs/exploration-2026-10-10.md`
has the store survey.

Store: futon1b (XTDB 2.1), but a **scratch** instance on 127.0.0.1:7093
(store `~/code/data/minus40/scratch-store`, bg.py job, 3G scope). The live
:7073 has not been touched.

## Done (all committed in ~/code/minus40, checks stated in the README)

1. **Lossless round trip.** Each memory file -> evidence entry + `:memory/assert`
   hyperedge (futon3c memory-write shape); `[[links]]` -> `:memory/link`. Export
   from the store is byte-identical for all 294 files; re-import is a no-op.

   transcripts (Write/Edit calls, Bash heredocs, file-history backups, `ls -l`
   listings, old-disk snapshot and birth times). One `:memory/version` edge per
   memory, put once per version with `:hx/valid-time`. Export as of now = live
   tree (294/294 byte-exact); as of 2026-10-06 = the pre-rebuild old disk
   (284/284). Claude Code re-stamps frontmatter after every Write/Edit; replay
   models that. Versions with unrecoverable text are marked "unknown content"
   rather than omitted.
3. **Sorries.** Candidate pairs by links and rare shared terms (631), judged by
   Haiku (Joe's choice) as conflict / restates / replaces / unrelated; a verdict
   only counts if both quotes are verbatim. 18 conflicts became sorries (futon3c
   `:challenge` shape + `:memory/sorry` edge); `list` and `discharge` work, and
   discharge keeps the open interval in history. None discharged (several are
   Joe's rules; ten touch WM/APM).
4. **Duplicate merges (proposals only).** 18 restates pairs -> 14 clusters -> 17
   alias proposals. Applying one puts an alias edge; reads resolve ids through
   it, nothing is rewritten; undo works; as-of before the apply shows them
   unmerged. None applied.
5. **Entities.** Rules (repos, seats, ports, a seed alias table) + a Haiku pass
   with verbatim surface forms -> 1,519 entities, 3,032 `:memory/mentions`
   edges in futon1b's entity table. `about phone1` resolves through aliases.

   some memories.

   `~/.claude/settings.json`) stats memory files and puts changed ones into the
   scratch store as exact versions. About 0.03 s idle; never fails the tool.

   versions are byte-exact.

- "At -40°, water thrown into the air turns into crystals before it hits the
  ground": structure should be added at write time, not by later batch passes.
- Do not reinvent 象: 小象 (classical draft at record time) and 大象 (classical
  reading of marked agent replies, joining a turn's commits, tracking open
  ports) already do the cheap tier and the ledger.
- Do not have a second agent read every agent turn; too heavy.

  a description step by step (math -> analysis -> complex analysis -> Green's
  function), not a directory lookup. codex-68's 3/2-category note
  (`futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/README-3halfs-categories.md`) has a vertical
  pasting operation with the same shape; I sent codex-68 a review of that note
  today (coverage is joint not per-leg; pasting needs a transport lemma along
  gluing isos; gluings lack a coherence condition).

  (Claude is currently off WM); the claude-14 session as a "your agent chat is
  a crime scene" case.

All against the scratch store; nothing restarts or reconfigures a live service.

| day | settled records | with evidence on :7073 |
|---|---|---|
| 10-04 | 162 | 139 |
| 10-05 | 319 | 73 |
| 10-06 | 42 | 8 |
| 10-09 | 512 | 0 |
| 10-10 | 204 | 0 |
| 10-11 | 46 | 0 |

Bell turns (status declared, origin agent) are never written, by design in the docstring. Ports are computed after the evidence write and stored only on the JSON record by `compute-ports!`, never in the evidence body. 939 of 3447 records carry ports. The claude-14 session has 47 records, 16 settled, none with ports and none with evidence. The operator turn itself is also already evidence on :7073 (the record's `evidence_id`, written by agent-chat/turn; 1486 records have one).

Before building a follower, send a discovery packet to whoever owns the turn service: why did the appends stop after the 10-06 reboot. On failure the service sets a health detail reading "futon1b busy; retrying", so that field is the first place to look. A file follower is still justified for what the existing path omits: bell turns and ports. Two design points keep it from becoming a second ledger. Mint the same id and body shape as `turn-evidence-entry`, so on switch-over to :7073 the appends are quiet duplicates rather than a parallel series. Do not add a memory-event record kind to turn-seam: the schema was derived from real operator turns and says so, and a memory version is not a turn. Join on session id and time instead. The memory evidence already carries `evidence/session-id` from the frontmatter stamp, and the turn evidence carries `:session-id` and tags the session, so one store answers "which turn wrote this version" without a new kind.

**Q2, model use.** The line is right and consistent with Joe's rule, because the agent-turn side is already classical: 大象 reads marks, 小象 drafts, and the only model tier is 象's reading of operator turns, which the turn service already dispatches. One constraint: the model read must not run inside the hook. The hook runs under Claude Code's 10 s timeout on every tool call. Record the version in the hook, run the entity read and conflict judge afterwards in a bg.py job, and attach the result to the same version id with the write's valid time. Water that freezes a few seconds after being thrown still freezes before it lands.

**Q3, duplication.** Four things. The turn evidence path above. The operator-turn evidence already on the record. Ports, where `turn_acts/turn-ports` over `session-acts` is the kernel, so the follower should read `:ports` from the record or call the same function rather than recompute, especially for the claude-14 records that have none. Per-turn open-port display, which `emacs/turn-stepper.el` already does; the cross-session aggregate by agent is new. For milestone 6 later, `agents/memory_mcp.clj` already exposes memory_record and memory_search.

**Q4, making the replay informative.** Decide the numbers before running and compute them for one or two control sessions of similar length, so "crime scene" can come out false. Candidates: open ports at session end and their age; accepted offers with no carrying-out commit, using the `:carries-out` link in `session-acts`; memory versions written in the session that later enter an open sorry; and the fraction of agent replies the classical tier can read at all (marks present, asks-operator). Since the claude-14 records have no ports and no evidence, the first measurement is how much of that session the existing machinery can reconstruct.

**Q5, hook risks.** I read the code; three concrete ones.
- The exclusive flock is held across the HTTP posts. If the scratch store hangs rather than refusing (a GC pause, the admission load the turn service already retries on), each changed file costs up to three posts at 3 s, the hook hits the 10 s timeout, and every other session's hook queues on the lock. Worst case is about 10 s added to every tool call in every session on zone. A refused connection is fast, so the store being down is fine. Fix: LOCK_NB and exit 0 when busy, or spool under the lock and post outside it.
- Mass deletion: anything that makes the glob return empty (HOME resolving differently in a service-run seat, a bad MINUS40_PROJECTS) marks every tracked memory deleted at now. Refuse deletions when `files` is empty or when they exceed some fraction.
- Attribution for step 2: a changed file is picked up by whichever session's tool call comes next. Use the stdin session id only when `tool_input` names that file. The frontmatter stamp already covers Write and Edit, so the payload adds information only for Bash heredocs.

**Q6, spot checks.** The live hook claim holds: the logged evidence id equals the sha of the current bytes and the version time equals the mtime to the millisecond. The quote check is whitespace-normalised, not byte-verbatim; say so. One sorry I read (agency-send-pass-mode-work vs agency-send-mode-brief-trap) gives the same instruction and differs only on the mechanism, a content classifier versus a fixed default, observed at two dates. So "conflict" currently covers disagreeing accounts, not only incompatible advice; a kind field on the sorry would help. One alias cluster (sidecar-build-standing-continue and wm-contract-standing-continue to those-are-fine-covers-the-sequence) merges three authorizations with different lanes and dates. Restates is right; alias would lose the scope of each. Suggest alias only when subject and scope match, and a restates edge as the final state otherwise. 293 versus 294 files is the minus40 memory added on 10-11, not an error.

**Other.** The follower should glob only `turn-*.json` with one dot; `.draft.json`, `.analysis.json` and `.turn-write-*.tmp` siblings sit in the same directory. About 1,100 of the 1,519 entities are singletons, mostly file paths, which are not entities in the spec's sense; fine for now, worth a kind filter in the `about` view.
